abortConditionsFromTheSecondAttempt.supersededBy: any of the three images at the archive, or the preservation manifest, failing its digest or byte-count check immediately before boot
abortConditionsFromTheSecondAttempt.why: It names five directories added to the image two attempts ago, which is not the image this record is about.  Carried forward it would sit in the list unable to trigger, which reads as a safeguard and is not one.  What it was for -- the loaded image being other than the one described -- is covered by the digest check, which is stricter because it compares the whole file.

appendOnly.policy: Records already sealed are bound here by digest and left byte-unchanged.
appendOnly.why: Two attempts and one spent production budget are recorded in files this one leans on.  A successor that edited any of them would be rewriting the evidence it claims to build on, and the digests below are what makes that visible rather than a matter of trust.

why.console=hvc0: the virtio console the host attaches. Without it the run produces no evidence in either direction.
why.init=/usr/lib/systemd/systemd: the real binary. /usr/sbin/init is a symlink to it, and naming the symlink adds a way for the boot to fail for a reason that is not about the image.
why.ro: matches the read-only attachment. The guest is refused writes at the device, and asking for them would only produce noise.
why.root=/dev/vda: the sealed image is a bare ext4 filesystem with no partition table, attached as the only block device.

bootAuthorisation.requiredBefore: any boot of this image -- one separate approval, given after this record has been reviewed, for the one run this record would judge
bootAuthorisation.whoApproves: the operator, in a separate instruction naming this record
bootAuthorisation.why: A document that set the exam and opened the run in the same breath would make the review it was written for impossible to fail: by the time anyone disagreed with a condition, the run would already be permitted.  Sealing the criteria first is what makes disagreement still able to change something.

earlierAttempts.why: It was made once against a different image and failed at PID 1.  Its allowance is gone and its verdict stands.

It was made once against a different image and passed, reaching its default target without the launcher's prerequisites being in reach.  Its allowance is gone, and this attempt does not extend it: a third image is a third exam.

gapsOpenAtTheSecondAttempt.closedBy: the account database staged into the image from native/etc, because the thing that would normally create it cannot write to a read-only root

This is recorded now so that refusal is a known result rather than a surprise, and so nobody later reads it as the image being broken.

host.why: MAC.3 is closed-local development work. The clean-Mac question is a different gate with a different environment, and this record does not touch it.

isolation.why: The guest is a filesystem built from 191 pinned packages and a launcher. It has no reason to reach the network or the host's files, and the cheapest way to keep a boot from becoming something else is to give it nothing to reach.

knownAbsentBeforeTheRun.consequence: everything the run learns, it learns from the console the host captures.  The guest cannot be asked a question and cannot answer one, so no receipt the guest produces is available to this run, and none is required by any condition here.

knownAbsentBeforeTheRun.consequence: the images survive a reboot and a temporary-directory sweep, and would not survive the loss of the machine.  It does not block a closed-local boot, which reads the files rather than risking them.

passConditions.condition: the three images loaded are the archived files at the paths, sizes and digests this record names, recomputed at the moment of loading rather than trusted from an earlier check
passConditions.judgedBy: the host reads each of the three files from the permanent archive, compares its byte count and its freshly computed sha256 with the values in subject.images, and recomputes the preservation manifest twice -- the copy inside the archive and the copy tracked in the repository -- against the digest in subject.preservationRecord.  Every one of these is taken immediately before the machine is configured, and any mismatch stops the run before a machine exists.  The results go into the run receipt.
passConditions.why: The image no longer lives only in a CI artifact that a workflow produced and would expire; it lives in an archive on a disk whose owner can change its permissions at any time.  A read-only mode prevents a slip, not a decision, so the only honest basis for saying these are the produced bytes is to hash them again at the moment they are used.

passConditions.condition: the machine is configured with no network device, no shared directory and no writable disk
passConditions.judgedBy: the configuration the host built is serialised into the run receipt and read back: the counts must be zero and the single disk attachment must be read-only

passConditions.condition: the run leaves a transcript that can be read by someone who was not there
passConditions.judgedBy: the whole console stream is written to a file, its sha256 and byte count go into the run receipt, and the file is kept whatever the verdict

passConditions.condition: every write the guest needs lands on tmpfs
passConditions.judgedBy: the mount table the guest executes is read from the image, and every path the launcher and its units write to is required to resolve to a tmpfs mount; the root disk being unchanged afterwards is the independent half of the same check.

passConditions.condition: this image is booted exactly once under this record, and the run that happens is the separately approved one
passConditions.judgedBy: the driver refuses to start when the receipt named by resultPath already exists, so the count is read off the filesystem rather than taken on trust; the receipt records the approval it ran under, and a second run of any kind is an abort condition rather than a retry.
passConditions.why: The production budget that made this image is spent and cannot be refilled.  A boot is not destructive by itself, but an attempt that could be quietly repeated until it passed would make the verdict meaningless, and the operator asked for exactly one.

passConditions.condition: PID 1 is the systemd that was built into this image
passConditions.judgedBy: the captured console shows systemd's own startup banner reporting version 255, which is the version the image carries

passConditions.condition: the guest kernel executes and mounts the sealed ext4 as its root filesystem
passConditions.judgedBy: the captured console shows the kernel banner and an EXT4-fs line naming the root device mounted read-only

passConditions.condition: the launcher executable matches the sealed fingerprint
passConditions.judgedBy: the digest is compared against the producer authority's sealed launcher block before the image is built, and the guest reports the digest of the file it actually executed once it can speak.

passConditions.condition: the launcher's own prerequisites pass inside the guest: the service account database resolves the identities it needs, the runtime rootfs is present, and it verifies against its sealed content manifest
passConditions.judgedBy: the captured console shows the launcher passing account resolution and passing the runtime rootfs verification against the sealed content manifest, with the manifest digest it reports equal to the value the production authority bound.  A refusal at either step is a failure of this condition rather than a known limit, because the material both steps look for is in this image.
passConditions.why: The second attempt recorded both of these as absent, so the launcher's refusal there was a known result and nothing was graded on it.  The successor image was produced to put them in.  With the material present, a refusal is a failure, and leaving the condition ungraded would let the one thing this image was made for go unchecked.

passConditions.condition: the launcher service starts on its own
passConditions.judgedBy: the console transcript has to show systemd starting the unit without a console command having asked for it, which the enablement symlink in the image is what produces.

passConditions.condition: the launcher runs as root as a least-privilege supervisor holding exactly the four sealed capabilities, and every checker and submission process it creates runs only after descent to a sealed unprivileged account
passConditions.judgedBy: in two halves that fail independently. The launcher half is read from the guest's own kernel status at startup, before the socket is bound: root in every identity slot, effective, permitted and bounding equal to the sealed four-capability mask, inheritable and ambient exactly zero. The submission half is read from the per-request setup order: the descent and its verification both precede the exec, the verification requires empty capability sets and no_new_privs on the child, and any stage failing stops the request before the exec rather than continuing past it.

passConditions.condition: the two files loaded are the ones two arm64 replicas independently converged on
passConditions.judgedBy: the host re-hashes the kernel and the root disk immediately before configuring the machine and refuses to start on any mismatch; both digests are written into the run receipt

passConditions.condition: no unit enters a failed state and the guest does not stall: the transcript shows continued progress to the readiness point rather than stopping at one
passConditions.judgedBy: the console transcript is read for any unit reported as failed, for any dependency or start-job timeout, and for a gap between its last line and the machine stopping that is longer than the run's own stated budget.  Any of the three is a failure.  A transcript that simply ends without reaching readiness counts as a stall rather than as an absence of evidence.
passConditions.why: Reaching a target and hanging on the way to it look alike in a transcript that is only searched for the words it hoped to find.  The operator asked for the absence of failure and freeze messages to be part of the exam, which makes the silence itself something that has to be judged.

passConditions.condition: no host wallet, model key or node secret is present in the guest
passConditions.judgedBy: the image is built from a fixed input list with no host path and no environment passthrough, and the produced image is searched for the known secret-bearing filenames and for the host's own wallet and key directories, which must have no entry.

passConditions.condition: the machine has no network device and no shared directory
passConditions.judgedBy: counted from the host virtual-machine configuration before the run starts, as the sealed boot receipt already counts them: zero network devices, zero shared directories, zero socket devices.

passConditions.condition: no authenticated host-guest transport, no node connection and no mining, reward, consensus or P2P authority is started, reached for or granted at any point in the run
passConditions.judgedBy: the machine configuration in the run receipt carries no network device, no shared directory and no socket device, so there is nothing for a transport to run over; the console transcript is read for any attempt to open one; and the receipt records that no node process was started and no reward, block, consensus or P2P authority was granted to the guest.  Reaching any of these is an abort, not a partial pass.
passConditions.why: MAC.4 is the next piece of work and its absence here is deliberate.  Writing it as a graded condition rather than as a note means a run that drifted into it would fail rather than be described afterwards as having gone further than planned.

passConditions.condition: no guest process, socket or temporary file survives the shutdown
passConditions.judgedBy: counted on the host after the run the way the sealed boot receipt counts host processes, extended to the socket path and the working directory; the guest's own tmpfs is gone with the machine by construction.

passConditions.condition: readiness and a clean shutdown are observed
passConditions.judgedBy: the launcher's own readiness point has to be visible to the host, which today it is not; making it visible is part of what this contract opens. The shutdown half is read from the console transcript.

passConditions.condition: the root disk stays read-only
passConditions.judgedBy: the disk is attached read-only by the host configuration, and its digest is taken before and after the run and required to be identical, the same way the sealed boot receipt established it.

passConditions.condition: the sealed root disk is byte-identical after the run
passConditions.judgedBy: the host re-hashes the root disk file after the machine stops and compares it with the digest in the green record. Read-only is a claim about the attachment; this is the check that the claim held, and it is the one condition the guest cannot fake.

passConditions.condition: systemd does not enter emergency and reaches its target
passConditions.judgedBy: read from the console transcript the run captures: the target it settles on is compared with the guest's own default, and any emergency or rescue unit appearing at all is a failure rather than a note.

readOnlyModeIsNotASecurityControl.whatFollows: The pass condition archive-digests-recomputed-immediately-before-boot exists for exactly this reason: the digests are computed again at the moment of loading, so what is trusted is the bytes read then rather than the permissions they were left under.
readOnlyModeIsNotASecurityControl.why: The archive is mode 0444 on files and 0555 on directories, owned by the account that made it.  That refuses a stray write, and it refuses nothing at all to whoever owns the files: a chmod is one command away, and no alarm follows it.  Reading the modes as protection would be reading a convenience as a guarantee.

recomputeImmediatelyBeforeBoot.how: Each file is read from the archive and hashed in full, its byte count compared with this record, and the archive's own manifest copy hashed against the repository's.  Nothing is cached from the preservation run: that check answered for the disk on the day it was made, and this one has to answer for the disk on the day it is used.

signing.why: the entitlement is what Virtualization.framework requires; an ad-hoc signature carries it on the machine that produced it and nowhere else, which is exactly the reach this work is allowed.

digestSourceForTheUnchangedCheck.field: subject.images, the row whose name is guest-root-disk, key sha256
digestSourceForTheUnchangedCheck.why: One carried condition compares the root disk after the run with a digest frozen before it.  Which document holds that digest has to be settled before the run rather than chosen afterwards, and it is this one: the same value the production run recorded and the preservation record archived, restated here and checked against both.

images.name: guest-initrd
images.role: the initial ramdisk the archive carries
images.whyUnused: the guest kernel has virtio-blk and ext4 built in rather than as modules, so it reaches the root filesystem without one.  It is archived and named here because it was produced by the same run, not because the boot needs it.

images.name: guest-root-disk
images.role: the sealed ext4 filesystem attached as the only block device

secondReplica.why: Two replicas were produced and both were preserved whole, and at the archive they are byte-identical.  That makes the second a recovery source for some later, separately approved run -- not a fallback inside this one.  Loading it after the first failed its digest would turn a detected corruption into a run that proceeded anyway, which is the opposite of what the check is for.

whatThisIs: The conditions a third closed-local boot would be judged by, written down before it is approved and before it is run.  Two attempts have been made against two earlier images: the first failed at PID 1 for a missing set of mount points, the second passed and stopped short of the launcher for want of material that image did not carry.  That material is in this image, which is why the launcher's own prerequisites are graded here for the first time.  The image itself no longer lives only in a CI artifact with an expiry: it sits in a permanent archive, which changes what has to be re-established at the moment of loading.  This record opens no run of its own; the approval is separate and comes after this has been read.
